item.title: Tupelo career center, Saltillo High and Mooreville Middle appear on TVA's STEM awards list
item.description: Tupelo Career Technical Center — Tupelo Water & Light Department. Saltillo High School — Tombigbee Electric Power Association. Mooreville Middle School — Tombigbee Electric Power Association. TVA groups recipients by the local power company. The workbook places Tupelo Career Technical Center under the Tupelo Water & Light Department. It lists Saltillo High School and Mooreville Middle School under Tombigbee Electric Power Association. Tupelo Public School District identifies its career center as the Tupelo Career-Technical Center. The classroom award list gives no individual grant amounts or descriptions. The district career center also has a separate reference to a robotics grant; the roster does not identify this classroom award as a robotics project. The Tennessee Valley Authority and Bicentennial Volunteers, Inc., its retiree organization, announced the regional awards on November 23, 2026. The 2026–27 list contains 334 school entries across the region, 36 in TVA's Mississippi district. The program awards $1.5 million regionwide and TVA estimates about 96,000 students will benefit across the region. The $5,000 figure is an upper limit for an individual award. It is not the amount awarded to a named school. Eligible schools receive electricity through a local power company served by TVA. The competitive process gives preference to proposals dealing with the environment, energy, economic development or solving community problems. The Tennessee STEM Innovation Network is a program partner and Battelle manages the network. TVA says that since 2018 the partners have provided more than $10.5 million through these awards, supporting more than 940,000 students across the region.
